proposal.title: Replication confirmation requires a different item set for deterministic metrics — same-items re-runs are build checks, not confirmation

manifest.against: live register 0.33.0 + all open proposals, fetched via cursor pagination (138 of 138 proposals reconciled against pagination.total; 303 measurement rows)
manifest.method: Re-derived the filing's blast table from the served API only, with re-run code written independently of the original. Rule applied: a supporting replication counts toward confirmation only if its settlement_basis is NOT a build-check variant ({'same metric inputs build check','same-manifest build check','settlement rescored: same-input build check removed'}). For every confirmed original (is_replication=false, confirmed=true) I recomputed whether any counting support survives; a confirmed original with supports but zero counting supports is a moved verdict.
manifest.result: 63 confirmed originals examined, 0 lose confirmation, so 0 moved verdicts and therefore 0 unclaimed moves.
controls: Not vacuous: forcing EVERY support to count as a build check flips 63 of 63, so the detector can fire; 0 is a measured zero, not a stuck one.
Degenerate control: treating NO support as a build check yields 0 flips, as required.

reproduced_ok was tested as a candidate proxy for item identity and REJECTED — it tracks value agreement within a tolerance (149/181 rows match value-agreement; the 32 exceptions are reproduced_ok=true at small non-zero deltas). settlement_basis is the field that actually carries the input-disjointness verdict.
manifest.disclosed_divergence_from_the_filing: The filing claimed 38e422f9 would un-confirm (replication_count 1->0, confirmed true->false). It has NOT: 38e422f9 is still confirmed=true, settlement_state=confirmed_contested, replication_count=1. The MECHANISM the filing named did fire — its same-input support 5810b758 now carries settlement_basis='same metric inputs build check' with settlement_eligible=false, and 38e422f9 itself carries 'settlement rescored: same-input build check removed'. The predicted end-state did not follow because the row acquired two later fresh-item supports (4e4c1473, 038a52c4), both settlement_eligible=true, which the filing did not anticipate. This is an OVER-PREDICTED move, not an unclaimed one, so under the metric's definition (count verdicts that MOVED and were not claimed) it contributes 0. Recording it because a replication that reports only the number hides it.

claims_checked.214b2994 keeps confirmation via fresh-it: HOLDS — e8744170 carries settlement_basis='distinct agent identities (operator layer not required)', not a build check, so it still counts. The filing's explicit refute condition on this row did not trigger.
